purpose: Canonical example for technical task quality. Use as a guide for evaluating technical tasks (infrastructure, technical debt, operations, research).

task.title: Database migration to PostgreSQL 16
task.why: PostgreSQL 15 reaches end-of-life in Q4/2027. Security patches will no longer be provided. We need to upgrade to maintain security compliance and access performance improvements in PostgreSQL 16 (15% faster query execution, improved JSON operations).
what: Upgrade PostgreSQL from version 15 to 16 on all environments (staging → production)
Verify application compatibility (run full integration test suite)
Update monitoring dashboards for new version metrics
Update runbooks and documentation with PostgreSQL 16-specific procedures

downtime.communication: Email to all customers 7 days in advance, status page update

risks: Schema incompatibilities may cause application errors
Migration may exceed planned downtime window
Rollback may be required if critical issues found

rollback.procedure: Restore from backup taken immediately before migration

technical.gherkin: Given the migration script runs on staging, when executed, then it completes without errors (exit code 0).
technical.measurement: Log file shows 'Migration completed successfully', no ERROR entries

technical.gherkin: Given the migration is complete, when the integration test suite runs, then 100% of tests pass within 5 minutes.
technical.measurement: CI pipeline shows 100% pass rate, total duration < 5 minutes

technical.gherkin: Given the production migration starts at 2 AM, when it completes, then total downtime is ≤ 2 hours.
technical.measurement: Downtime monitoring shows ≤ 120 minutes from start to service restoration

technical.gherkin: Given the rollback procedure is documented, when tested on staging, then it completes within 45 minutes.
technical.measurement: Rollback test log shows completion in ≤ 45 minutes

documentation.description: Monitoring dashboard updated with new PostgreSQL 16 metrics

requires: On-call engineer scheduled for migration weekend

business: Performance improvement: 15% faster average query time
Zero customer-reported incidents related to migration

technicalScope.evidence: Clear 'what' section with 5 specific work items, each actionable and testable.

justification.evidence: Clear 'why' section with EOL date, security impact, and performance benefits quantified.

impactAnalysis.evidence: Lists all affected systems, planned downtime with communication plan, and specific risks.

rollbackPlan.evidence: Documented procedure, tested on staging, estimated time (45 min), location of runbook.

acPresence.evidence: 6 acceptance criteria: 4 technical (TC1-TC4) + 2 documentation (DC1-DC2). Covers success, compatibility, downtime, rollback.

acTestability.evidence: All AC are SMART: Specific (exit code 0), Measurable (100% pass rate, ≤ 2 hours), Achievable, Relevant, Testable.

dependencies.evidence: Documents blocks (#15), relatedTo, and requires (backup, approval, on-call).

sizeRisk.evidence: Well-scoped with clear boundaries. Risks identified. Estimated: L (large) due to production impact.

whyThisIsReferenceQuality: Quantifies everything: downtime (2h), test pass rate (100%), rollback time (45min), performance gain (15%).
Rollback plan is not just documented but tested – critical for production changes.
Acceptance criteria cover technical success, compatibility, operational constraints, and documentation.
Dependencies explicitly documented (blocks, requires) for coordination with other teams.
Success metrics include both technical (zero data loss) and business (security compliance, performance) outcomes.
Uses Gherkin syntax for technical AC – makes them testable by automation.
howToUseThisReference: Use as a template for structuring technical tasks: why → what → impact → AC → dependencies.
Compare your task against this reference: Do you have a clear 'why' with quantified impact?
Check if your acceptance criteria are as specific and measurable as this reference.
Ensure you have a tested rollback plan for any production-impacting change.
Document dependencies (blocks/requires) to coordinate with other teams.
Use the quality criteria checklist to self-assess before refinement.
differencesFromStory: No 'As a [user]...' format – tasks use imperative style ('Upgrade PostgreSQL...').
No business value in 'so that...' form – value is indirect (security, performance, stability).
Focus on technical outcomes (exit code 0, 100% tests pass) vs. user outcomes (download within 3 seconds).
Requires rollback plan – stories typically don't need this.
Impact section critical – stories focus on user benefit, tasks on system impact.
